correctness.rationale: The proof verifies both regimes including equality and strict positivity. Dominant-coordinate deletion is an onto isometry. Balanced coordinate facets have explicit relative-interior witnesses, yielding exactly 2n dual extreme points. Their unique positive linear circuit forces a dual isometry to have a common sign and weight-matching permutation. The converse, facet-count separation, and group formula are established. The standalone exact checker passed 441 rational weight representatives; this is supporting finite evidence, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text sections and targeted scientific searches reveal no statement classifying all strictly positive weighted sup-norm hyperplanes up to linear isometry or recovering the normalized weight multiset. Sohel–Sain–Paul Theorem 2.8 addresses facet counts and minimal cubical embedding, which alone do not identify isometry classes among noncubical hyperplanes. The other close paper addresses extreme contractions, and the closest published search hits address different spaces/invariants. A broader theorem on minimal-representation uniqueness remains the main bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: An older general theorem that every isometry between irredundant finite cubical representations extends to a signed permutation may subsume the balanced-case criterion.
The primary-literature search cannot exclude unindexed or inaccessible equivalent classifications.

value.rationale: The natural class of all strictly positive codimension-one real ℓ∞ hyperplanes is completely classified up to isometry in every n≥3. The result recovers continuous intrinsic weight ratios and determines all automorphisms, while showing a sharp dominance transition to one cubical type. It addresses invariant moduli and symmetry, not a chosen low-dimensional numerical curiosity or an arbitrary slice.
